name="jinjacho">[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4402102 Habuhimenomikoto Shrine] - Shizuoka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines</ref> {{nihongo|'''Habuhime Shrine (Shimoda)'''|波布比咩命神社 (下田市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

== Overview ==
The shrine is situated immediately north of the east exit of {{ill|Izukyū Shimoda Station|Q6102244|qid=Q6102244}}, about a one-minute walk away, and directly north of Shimoda City Hall (Higashi-Hongo Office).

Habuhimenomikoto Shrine is considered a disputed candidate for designation as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, along with Ōtsunoyukinomikoto Shrine. With regard to the former, it is often interpreted as a branch shrine and remote place of worship of the Habuhimenomikoto Shrine located just south of {{ill|Port of Habu|Q11555565|qid=Q11555565}} on the southeastern side of {{ill|Izu Ōshima|Q1070580|qid=Q1070580}}, which is regarded as the main shrine.<ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140102-02.html Habuhimenomikoto Shrine] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>

Shimoda was once a deeply indented inlet, and the shrine grounds were formerly a small island. During the Kamakura period, a deity known as “Funato Myōjin” was enshrined there, and it is said that the shrine later became Habuhime Shrine.<ref name="yuisho">Shrine grounds origin inscription</ref>

During the Edo period, the shrine was known as “Ukishima-sama” (Floating Island Deity). It is said that during the {{ill|1854 Tōkai earthquake|Q3742363|qid=Q3742363}}, large ships were washed ashore, but the shrine grounds themselves were not flooded.<ref name="yuisho"/>

* Habuhimenomikoto
